Population increased in Swansea

The estimated population of Swansea in 2024 was 251,304 usual residents, a rise of 0.9% since 2023.

This meant that Swansea's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Swansea increased by 5.6%.

Over this slightly longer period, Swansea was also among the 20% fastest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Swansea

The average (median) age fell to 40.2 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Swansea has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Swansea is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Swansea's population of 251,304 usual residents was made up of:

  • 42,002 people aged 0 to 15 years, (16.7%)
  • 158,335 people aged 16 to 64 years, (63%)
  • 50,967 people aged 65 years and over, (20.3%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Swansea has a slightly lower proportion of people aged 0 to 15 years (16.7% compared with 18.3% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Swansea, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Swansea
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Swansea, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 663 people (-0.3%). In total, there were 2,030 births and 2,693 deaths in Swansea.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 1,863 (-0.7%). There were 10,712 people entering the area and 12,575 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Swansea's population of 4,909 (2%) as a result of 6,971 people entering the area and 2,062 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Swansea was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Swansea in mid-2023 is 248,959.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 2,148 people and internal migration estimates were revised upwards by 69 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 2,217 people.
